questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) The list of items
(b) are kept
(c) in the drawer.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) She has been
(b) working here
(c) since five years.
questions.explanation: A length of time takes "for": "for five years".

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) Neither of the boys
(b) have finished
(c) their homework.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) He is more smarter
(b) than his brother
(c) in mathematics.
questions.explanation: Do not use "more" with "smarter": it is a double comparative.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) I am looking forward
(b) to meet
(c) you next week.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) Scarcely had he
(b) entered the room
(c) than the lights went out.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) She gave me
(b) a good advice
(c) on the topic.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) Each of the students
(b) were given
(c) a certificate.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) He did not
(b) know where
(c) was the station.
questions.explanation: Use statement order after "where": "where the station was".

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) The sun
(b) rises
(c) in the east.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) I prefer tea
(b) than coffee
(c) in the morning.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) Though he was tired
(b) but he
(c) finished the work.
questions.explanation: "Though" and "but" should not be used together.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) The furniture
(b) in the office
(c) are old.

Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is none, choose "No error".

(a) She asked me
(b) that where
(c) I was going.
questions.explanation: A reported question does not use "that": "where I was going".
